thread.title: Gold set to post back-to-back gains as stocks extend wobbly start to the year

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Gold set to post back-to-back gains as stocks extend wobbly start to the year
text:
Gold futures on Thursday extended a climb toward its highest level in about six months as U.S. stocks staged sharp pullback and as the dollar softened.
February gold on Comex GCG9, +0.44% gained $6.10, or 0.5%, to t $1,290.30 an ounce, after the commodity closed 0.2% higher in the prior session and marked it highest finis since middle of June, according to FactSet data.
Gold looked set to score a second straight gain as a bearish revenue outlook from iPhone-maker Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.11% rattled markets, with investors poised to push the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.46% sharply lower and the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.08% and the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.13% also set to open down.
Apple shares headed lower after the tech giant announced a rare cut to its sales forecast, citing sluggish economic growth in China, which could also be exacerbated by the longstanding tariff dispute between Beijing and Washington.
Apple’s late-Wednesday announcement has provided further evidence that the world’s second largest economy is on an uneven footing, which could deliver fresh worries of contraction in international economic expansion, market participants said.
Equity market jitters to start 2019 and growing expectations of a pause in coming rate increases by the Federal Reserve, which has become more cognizant of the market’s tailspin lower , has helped support bullion prices.
“After months of indecision, gold appears to be in a clearly defined uptrend. Yes, it’s overbought, but it has been that way for week,” wrote Stephen Todd, editor and publisher of financial blog Todd Market Forecast, in a Thursday report.
Meanwhile, silver, a precious metal that tends to be more sensitive to signs of global economic weakness punched higher after healthy private-sector employment data from ADP.
March silver SIH9, +0.45% was picking up 5 cents, or 0.3%, to reach $15.70, after trading lower earlier Thursday. Silver closed up 0.7% on Wednesday.
Automatic Data Processing Inc. ADP, -0.75% showed that 271,000 private-sector jobs were added in December, compared with a previous monthly reading of 179,000.
Market participants are awaiting the more closely followed nonfarm-payroll report on Friday, with 184,000 jobs expected in December and an unemployment rate at 3.6%.
Mark DeCambre Mark DeCambre is MarketWatch's markets editor. He is based in New York. Follow him on Twitter @mdecambre.
